data.title: Trump says Democrats facing veto power should work with him
data.description:
By Bo Erickson and Katharine Jackson

US President Donald Trump pledged on Friday to veto legislation passed by Democrats when they take control of Congress in 2027, but said his veto power should be seen as a starting point for lawmakers who want to achieve change.

Speaking at a White House news conference, Trump called the presidential veto "extreme powers," and said his threat to block legislation would cause Democrats to moderate their policies.

"They're going to send things my way, and I'm going to veto them. And then they're going to send more things, and I'm going to veto them," Trump said. "And they could go two years and one month, because that's what we have, and I'm going to veto them."

Trump said Democrats may realize that to avoid his veto, they could work with him to accomplish legislative goals.

"Because of the power of the veto, there's a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done," he said.

Trump said many Democrats had called him to discuss healthcare and immigration reform and pointed to healthcare as an area where lawmakers from different perspectives might meet somewhere in the middle.

"I'm open to great healthcare now, especially on healthcare. I'm open to great healthcare now," he said.

"Can it be what they want? No, but it can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country."

With the new Congress set to choose its leadership soon, Trump described Senator Chuck Schumer, who is vying to become senate majority leader, and Representative Hakeem Jeffries, who is on the path to becoming the next house speaker, both from New York, as "smart" and expressed willingness to work together.

"If they want to get things done, I want to get things done too," Trump said.

Trump also said Democratic Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa had called him two days ago about the border and he thought they could find a solution.

"She was really nice. It was a very productive call, and she wants to have a strong border. And we'll be able. I think we'll be able to work something out," he said.

data.title: SEC Proposes to Bring Securities Reporting Platform Under Direct Supervision
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

The Securities and Exchange Commission is proposing to restructure the system where securities exchanges report trading data.

The proposal aims to change the Consolidated Audit Trail, which is a centralized database that tracks trading activity across securities exchanges.

The SEC has proposed to rescind Rule 613, which requires securities exchanges to report their trading activity to the CAT. In its place, the SEC proposes to require exchanges to report the same information directly to the SEC or its designee.

The move would bring the CAT under the SEC's direct control.

SEC Chair Paul Atkins has been reviewing the CAT and approving amendments that have reduced its annual operating costs by more than $100 million. Atkins has also permanently eliminated the reporting of personally identifiable information to the CAT.

The proposal addresses concerns about the CAT's funding and would put the database on sustainable footing, Atkins said.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: FDA must pay legal fees to group that won court fight over COVID vaccine records
data.description:
By Mike Scarcella

A federal judge on Friday awarded more than $571,000 in legal fees to an organization of public health professionals, scientists and others that sued the US Food and Drug ​Administration to obtain COVID-19 vaccine approval records.

US District Judge Mark Pittman in Fort Worth, Texas, said the FDA must pay Public Health and Medical Professionals for Transparency fees for the work of their lawyers at Siri & Glimstad in a public records lawsuit that led to the disclosure of more than 1.8 million records. The judge formally closed the case on Friday.

The lawsuit garnered national attention after the FDA said it would take decades to process the records, drawing a rebuke from ​the judge and an order requiring a much faster timeline.

The ​group sued the FDA in 2021 seeking information the agency relied on to approve the Pfizer-BioNTech coronavirus vaccine. Pfizer ​was not a defendant but participated in the litigation to protect its business information.

“It should not have required over 1,600 hours billed across 22 attorneys and staff for the FDA to do what it should have done from the start — be transparent and release to the public the documents it relied upon to license Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine,” the plaintiff's attorneys, Aaron Siri and Elizabeth Brehm, said on Friday.

The FDA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Pittman in a ruling against the FDA said in 2024 “the COVID-19 pandemic is ​long passed and so has any legitimate reason for concealing from the American people the information relied upon by the government in approving the Pfizer vaccine."

The FDA’s compliance with Pittman’s orders showed “that its initial protestations lacked a reasonable basis,” the plaintiffs said in a court filing. “This is unsurprising, given the federal government is one of the most powerful and well-funded entities on the planet.”

The plaintiff had asked the court to award $854,000 in fees. Some portion of the fee award will be paid to an unidentified outside litigation funder, the plaintiff’s lawyers told the court. Such funders provide financing in exchange for a share ​of a case’s proceeds.

The case is Public Health and Medical Professionals for Transparency v. U.S. Food and Drug Administration, US District Court for the Northern District of Texas, No. 4:21-cv-01058-P.

For plaintiff: ⁠Aaron Siri ​and Elizabeth Brehm of Siri & Glimstad

For defendant: Andrew Freidah of the US ​Justice Department

data.title: S&P 500 plunges to a 7-month low and breaks back below 7,000
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) has firmly entered correction territory, now trading -11.2% below its all-time high of 7,844.52 set on October 6.

On Friday afternoon the benchmark index was down -3%, slipping back below the psychologically important 7,000 level to trade near 6,950.

That marks its lowest point since April 14. Heading into the close, the S&P 500 was also lower by -7.8% for the week, underscoring the breadth and intensity of the recent selling pressure.

Much of the decline has been concentrated in the technology sector, which carries substantial weight in the index. Nvidia , the S&P 500’s largest holding, has been a primary driver of the weakness. Shares of the chipmaker were down -12.8% and trading at their lowest level in more than a year, a level last seen in May 2025.

The sharp drop in Nvidia and other high-profile technology names has amplified the broader market’s move lower, pulling the index into its first correction of the current cycle and leaving investors focused on whether support near current levels can hold.

data.title: Honda recalls 810,592 US vehicles over Takata airbag inflators
data.description:
Honda will recall 810,592 vehicles in the United States to replace Takata airbag inflators that could potentially experience propellant degradation, the automaker said on Friday

The recall covers certain 2012-2013 Honda Civic and CR-V models, 2013 Honda Accord, 2013 Acura ILX, and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 US states and territories.

The affected vehicles are equipped with front driver and/or passenger airbag inflators containing a moisture-absorbing desiccant. Honda said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators in regions with high temperatures, humidity, and significant temperature fluctuations.

The company said no inflator ruptures, injuries, or fatalities have been reported in connection with the newly recalled inflator types.

Honda will replace the affected inflators free of charge. Mailed notifications to vehicle owners are scheduled to begin in December 2026.

Owners can check their vehicle's recall status through Honda and Acura's recall websites or by calling the company's dedicated recall helpline, Honda said.

data.title: U.S. Approves 879,000 AI Chips To China
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies, including Alibaba (BABA) and Tencent (0700.HK), through May 2026, according to documents released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee on Thursday.

Some approvals involved companies designated by the U.S. Department of Defense as Chinese Military Companies.

The committee said businesses submitted approximately 3.4 million requests between December and May to sell U.S. made AI chips to China, including products from Nvidia (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). The approvals have raised concerns among lawmakers over the enforcement of export restrictions and potential national security risks.

Both Nvidia and AMD said they comply with U.S. export control regulations. Nvidia said the licensing process involved multiple government agencies and strict conditions, adding that it had since stopped shipping H200 chips to China.

The company reported $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from licensed chip sales to China, although shipments to the country accounted for less than 1 percent of its data centre revenue in the previous quarter.

The documents also identified license applications involving ByteDance, Baidu (BIDU) and Tesla's Shanghai operations. Lawmakers are seeking tighter restrictions amid concerns that advanced U.S. chips could reach Chinese entities through intermediaries.

data.title: Fitness Champs Holdings Limited Announces Closing of $5 Million Public Offering and Addresses Nasdaq Deficiency Notice
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Fitness Champs Holdings Limited (“Fitness Champs Holdings”, “FCHL” or the “Company”) , a distinguished aquatic sports education provider in Singapore, today announced that the closing of its previously announced best-efforts public offering (the “Offering”) with gross proceeds to the Company expected to be approximately $5 million, before deducting placement agent fees and other estimated expenses payable by the Company, excluding any proceeds from the exercise of the Warrants (as defined below). The Company intends to use the net proceeds from this Offering for business expansion, general working capital purposes and other general corporate purposes. The Company believes that, as a result of the Offering, it has regained compliance with the stockholders’ equity requirement of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) to address the previously reported deficiency, as discussed further below.

The Offering

The Offering is comprised of 14,285,715 units (each a “Unit”), consisting of one Class A ordinary share of the Company, par value $0.00225 per share (the “Class A Ordinary Shares”), or in lieu thereof, a pre-funded warrant, and one warrant to purchase one Class A Ordinary Share (each, a “Warrant”). The public offering price of the Units is $0.35 per Unit. Each of the Warrants has an exercise price of $1.02 per Class A Ordinary Share and be exercisable beginning immediately upon issuance and will expire on the six-month anniversary of the issuance date.

We are registering 14,285,715 Class A Ordinary Shares underlying the Pre-Funded Warrants and 14,285,715 Class A Ordinary Shares underlying the Warrants. Each of the Pre-Funded Warrants will have an exercise price of $0.00225 per Class A Ordinary Share and will be immediately exercisable (subject to the beneficial ownership limitation) and may be exercised at any time until all of the Pre-Funded Warrants are exercised in full.

A holder of the Warrants may, at any time and in its sole discretion, exercise its Warrants in whole or in part by means of a “zero exercise price” option. As a result of this feature, we do not expect to receive any cash proceeds from the exercise of the Warrants because it is highly unlikely that a Warrant holder will elect to pay an exercise price in cash to receive Class A Ordinary Shares when they could elect the “zero exercise price” option in these circumstances to receive more Class A Ordinary Shares than they would receive if they did pay an exercise price. Under the zero-exercise price option, a holder of a Warrant will receive up to fifteen (15) Class A Ordinary Shares for each Warrant without paying any exercise price to us. It is anticipated that all Warrant holders will utilize the zero-exercise price option as this allows for the exercise of the Warrants for no additional consideration and will result in a greater number of Class A Ordinary Shares that investors will receive upon exercise than what would be issuable upon cash exercise or cashless exercise. As a result, there is no practical or financial incentive for holders of the Warrants to exercise the Warrants via cash exercise or cashless exercise and we do not expect to receive any proceeds from the exercise of the Warrants overall. If all 14,285,715 Warrants are exercised under the zero-exercise price option, we would issue an aggregate of 214,285,725 Class A Ordinary Shares for no additional consideration.

Univest Securities, LLC is acting as sole placement agent for the offering.

The securities described above were offered by the Company pursuant to a registration statement on Form F-1 (File No. 333-299806), as amended, and declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on November 13, 2026. This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to the registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. The Offering was made only by means of a written preliminary prospectus and final prospectus that will form a part of the registration statement. The final prospectus relating to the offering has been filed with the SEC and is available on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov. Electronic copies of the final prospectus relating to this offering may be obtained, when available, by contacting Univest Securities, LLC at info@univest.us, or by calling +1 (212) 343-8888.

Stockholders’ Equity Requirement

As previously reported on a Form 6-K, on May 26, 2026, the Company received a letter from Nasdaq indicating that it was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), because (i) the stockholders’ equity of the Company of $598,490 as of December 31, 2025, as reported in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025, was below the minimum stockholders’ equity requirement of $2,500,000 (the “Nasdaq Equity Requirement”) and (ii) the Company did not, as of May 26, 2026, meet the alternatives standards of market value of listed securities or net income from continuing operations for compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rules 5550(b)(2) and 5550(b)(3), respectively. The Company submitted a plan to regain compliance and was granted 180 calendar days from May 26, 2026 (or until November 20, 2026), to evidence compliance.

Based on the proceeds of funds from the Offering, the Company believes that, as of the date of this press release, it has stockholders’ equity in excess of the Nasdaq Equity Requirement. However, the final determination of compliance is subject to review and approval by Nasdaq. If at any time during the next periodic report the Company does not evidence compliance, the Company may be subject to delisting.

If, at the time of the Company’s next periodic report, the Company is deemed by Nasdaq not to be in compliance, the Company would have the right to request a hearing before a Nasdaq hearings panel pursuant to the procedures set forth in the applicable Nasdaq Listing Rules. However, there can be no assurance that, if the Company does appeal any delisting determination that such appeal would be successful.

While the Company believes it now is compliance with the Nasdaq Equity Requirement, if Nasdaq determines it is not in compliance, the Company will take all reasonable measures available to regain compliance under the Nasdaq Listing Rules and remain listed on Nasdaq. There can be no assurance that Nasdaq will determine that the Company (i) has regained compliance with the Nasdaq Equity Requirement, (ii) will maintain compliance with the Nasdaq Equity Requirement, or (iii) will maintain compliance with the other Nasdaq continued listing requirements or be successful in appealing any delisting determination.

About Fitness Champs Holdings Limited

Fitness Champs Holdings Limited is a distinguished aquatic sports education provider, offering general swimming lessons to children and adults, with ladies-only swimming lessons available, as well as aquatic sports classes such as competitive swimming and lifesaving. The Company is one of the largest providers of swimming lessons to children enrolled in public schools under the Ministry of Education of Singapore in Singapore through the SwimSafer program, and has been offering private swimming lessons to children, youths and adults under its brand “Fitness Champs” since 2012. The Company aims to make swimming an enjoyable and affordable sport for children and adults, for water safety and as a way of keeping fit and healthy. Fitness Champs also plans to grow into a diversified sports education provider by expanding its offerings to include other sports such as pickleball. For more information, please visit the Company’s website at https://ir.fitnesschamps.sg/.

data.title: European emissions proposal faces Middle East pushback at UN aviation agency
data.description:
By Allison Lampert

Plans to change the European Union's Emissions Trading System faced pushback at a global aviation gathering that wraps up on Friday, as Middle East countries challenged fresh efforts to curb pollution from airlines outside an existing deal.

It is the latest revolt within the aviation sector over plans to expand Europe's biggest climate change policy to cover flights to third-country destinations within 5,000 km (3,107 miles) of Frankfurt Airport, starting in 2029. The ETS currently applies to flights within the European Economic Area.

Saudi Arabia urged International Civil Aviation Organization member countries to support a global approach to countering emissions under the decade-old Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation. Saudi Arabia wants CORSIA, an ICAO program that is mandatory for most airlines, to be the only emissions plan covering international aviation.

Qatar also proposed that ICAO undertake a technical assessment of the implications of the EU ETS for CORSIA.

Several European countries disagreed with the two Middle East countries' positions.

Under CORSIA, airlines in most countries have to buy offsets in environmental projects to counter their rising emissions from international flights.

The airline industry has pledged to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, but executives acknowledge the target will be difficult to hit due to shortages of green jet fuel and increasing passenger traffic.

Airlines and most countries support CORSIA to avoid a patchwork of emissions programs that they argue would raise costs. But some European lawmakers and environmental groups have argued CORSIA does not go far enough to reduce international aviation emissions.

Under the EU proposal, the 5,000-km distance would cover flights to airports in the Middle East and North Africa but omit transatlantic flights to the United States.

Saudi Arabia, supported by Kuwait, Qatar and Egypt, urged countries and regional organizations to avoid overlapping and double charging under "duplicative or extraterritorial emissions trade schemes that will increase compliance costs, create administrative burdens and distort competition."

ICAO cannot impose rules on its 193 member states, but its decisions influence national regulations.

The ICAO assembly also elected Ethiopia, Oman, Turkey and Indonesia to join its governing council, which will now have 40 countries, up from 36.

data.title: Anthropic's Share Count May Be Even Higher, Columbia Prof Says — WSJ
data.description:
By Telis Demos

Counting Anthropic's shares isn't simple. The basic count and the fully diluted count results in market values that differ by hundreds of billions of dollars.

Some investors and analysts have been using a fully diluted count outlined in the prospectus. That count, around 18 billion, is billions more shares than the roughly 13 billion basic tally-or in market value terms, about $1.6 trillion versus $1.2 trillion at recent share prices.

But according to Columbia Business School auditing and accounting professor Shivaram Rajgopal, there is a case to be made for using an even larger sharecount figure.

Rajgopal, in a post this week, writes that his count of "everything that can plausibly turn into stock" is around 21 billion shares. The analysis was based on a $97 share price, roughly Thursday's close of $97.17.

His expanded count included several adjustments, such as potential further issuance to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund over the next decade, plus shares reserved for employee donation matching beyond what is already tied to vested equity, as well as shares that could be issued to settle some $67 billion of financing from Amazon, Google and Broadcom.

Rajgopal writes that when calculating earnings per share, or EPS, "there is no single right S for Anthropic. The fairer approach is to show the range and say which S you are using."

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: AI tech rout prompts US investors to rush into value stocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq now down almost 2% year to date, was up 19% YTD in October
  • More Fed rate hikes seen pressuring growth stocks near term
  • Median S&P 500 stock up 7% in 2026, index up only 2% so far

By Noel Randewich, Caroline Valetkevitch and Sinéad Carew

putting down for a tweak -dg

Wall Street fled headlong on Friday from the AI boom to the relative safety of bonds and lower-priced shares outside the tech sector.

Technology carnage was extensive. Anthropic’s sharp decline took it within a whisker of its IPO price before recovering to trade down 10%, just a day after a record debut that briefly valued the AI lab above $2 trillion. The Nasdaq composite was down over 4% for its third decline of 2% or more this week, its biggest weekly decline since last year’s Liberation Day rout. The pullback put it lower for the year for the first time since April.

The Nasdaq is now down almost 2% in 2026, relinquishing an annual gain of almost 19% through early October.

The retreat partly reflects expectations that high inflation readings will force the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in coming months, likely further increasing borrowing costs and compressing valuations – and making Treasuries and so-called value stocks look like a better bet.

“Yesterday’s AI IPO is a valuation test, and with the 10-year around 5% and the Fed still hiking, investors are asking how much of the AI story is already priced in,” said Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera, El Segundo, California.

Friday’s action highlights the shift in fortunes on Wall Street since the Nasdaq hit its last high on October 6. A handful of AI-related heavyweights had accounted for most of the S&P 500’s gains for much of 2026, masking underwhelming returns from the index’s other components.

But the median S&P 500 CBOE:SPX stock now is up almost 7% in 2026. That beats the 2% year-to-date gain in the S&P 500, which has been hobbled of late by a 46% slump in Nvidia and deep declines in other AI stocks, including a 12% drop in Broadcom on Friday.

The rotation away from tech is making winners out of a sector that has long been overlooked: value stocks that trade at lower multiples to their earnings and net worth than the growth stocks that soared during the AI boom.

“Kevin Warsh represents a different approach to monetary policy, and that has introduced additional uncertainty regarding interest rates, inflation, and economic growth,” said Philip Palumbo, CEO of Palumbo Wealth Management. “Markets do not like uncertainty, and right now we have plenty of it.“

The S&P 500 value index is up 8% in 2026, compared to a 2% drop in the S&P 500 growth index (.IGX). The switch puts cautious value investing on track to beat growth for the first time since 2022, when inflation fears sent Wall Street into its worst slump since the 2008 financial crisis.

Many analysts and portfolio managers said they did not view the AI trade as impaired. Instead, they said, an occasional washout can improve valuations and draw in investors with a longer-term perspective.

“You have a confluence of short-term negative factors,” said Jim Awad, senior managing director at Clearstead Advisors LLC in New York. He pointed to questions about the health of the underlying business at Nvidia , the onetime market leader whose shares have been in free fall since the Nasdaq composite hit its most recent record in October, shedding more than $2.2 trillion of market value.

“The fundamentals have not deteriorated as much as the stock prices have,” Awad said. “I would view it just as a normal violent correction in a long-term upward trend in AI spending and in the markets.”

Meanwhile, the flight to value stocks and Treasury notes, which rallied sharply on Friday, is the latest sign of markets grappling with the extent to which a slowing buildout of AI infrastructure will hit US growth – a debate that has been going on all year, if not to this extreme.

"This is your classic flight-to-safety trade. So as investors are getting a little bit more concerned about the AI trade, they're moving out of those stocks and into Treasury securities,” said Lawrence Gillum, chief fixed-income strategist at LPL Financial. “Anytime there's been some sort of hiccup in the AI trade, we've seen the Treasury market rally on the back of that."

data.title: US measles cases near 6,000 mark as outbreak worsens
data.description:
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday reported 5,838 measles cases as of November 19, as the country battles its worst outbreak of the viral infection in decades.

  • Measles cases in the US have climbed above 5,000 for the first time since 1991. Earlier this week, US lost its measles elimination status after 26 years

  • Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, reported an eighth measles-related death and confirmed 1,631 measles cases including 326 hospitalizations, as of November 20

  • Wisconsin has reported two deaths, while New York state recorded its first measles-associated ‌death, involving a child

  • The CDC has confirmed six measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, though it does not specify the states where the deaths were recorded

  • The gap in numbers follows a policy shift under U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., with the CDC switching to the National Center for Health Statistics' mortality data to track measles deaths, replacing its earlier reliance on state health departments' figures.
